doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Real medicine, diet and the new millennium
summary: Criticizes modern medicine, praises Hippocrates and diet, and predicts cosmic and political change.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: medicine, he never operated on anybody, and treated nervous disorders with higher mathematics. Because numbers quiet the nervous system. Because numbers are what everything is made of. There’s a book in the Bible called “Numbers.” So if you get interested in the numerical aspect of anything, your nerves quiet down. This is medicine.
So you’d be a believer in what we call alternative medicine?

Alternative medicine is the tip of the iceberg. Every doctor of any consequence would be a dietician. Because that’s the root of all sickness. The wrong foods that we put into our bodies. They make us sick. And it’s ridiculous to talk of keeping people healthy while you’re selling them the very food that’s making them sick. That’s cold. Medicine has got to change, and I think it will in this new millennium. I think a new millennium is a cosmic changing. It wipes out the old and starts a new structure. I think we’re seeing that happen. Politically — I called the election in England that put the Labor Party into power. Everybody thought I was nuts. I called the election in France that put the Socialists predominantly in the Senate, although Chirac remains President, but he’s a figurehead, because the Socialists have the most seats. And Lionel Jospin runs the country. And I called the defeat of Helmut Kohl. And I’m calling the defeat of the Republicans in the year 2000. They’re finished.
